What was wrong in the previous version

The previous PDF (153 pages, sent on 21 Nov 2026) built the dps.db parts of the API cards by reading the code. That counted every table any branch might touch, and once counted a settings object as a saved row. Every API section is now built from real runs of the DPS code on an empty test database. These are the differences found so far (Stage 1: the APIs of steps 1-14; Stage 2: catalogue, health and operations; Stage 3: the APIs outside DPS, where the requests DPS really sends matched the contract and no row was wrong).

Old pageAPIThe old PDF saidA real run shows
8, 103POST /dps/v1/batchesThe answer shows "status": "COMPLETED".A new batch answers RUNNING. COMPLETED comes back at once only when every file is a duplicate or refused.

The other tables change only when the last field is decided (job DONE, notice); label memory and approved figures only for statements.

21, 103-106POST /dps/v1/batches/{batchId}/rerunAlways changes dps_job and dps_batch.Only the audit line is new when no item has died. dps_job and dps_batch change only when there are DEAD items.

How to read it

  • API cards: the header colour is the party that owns the API (DPS teal, Spring blue, DMS amber). POST sends data; GET reads data. The From → to chips use the same colours.
  • Code blocks: copied from the file, with its real line numbers on the left; the teal text on the right of a line explains that line (it is not in the file).
  • JSON: field names in navy, text in green, numbers in orange, the explanation of each line in grey on the right.
  • Stored: the box takes the colour of where it is saved: green = dps.db, amber = the DMS store, teal = DPS's own files (derived\), blue = Spring. Not stored (grey) = only in memory during the job. Grey boxes without a label are tips.
  • "If" boxes (violet): what changes in that sub-step for another path; the path map after step 14 lists them all. Violet is used for nothing else.
  • DB tables: green headers, because they live in dps.db; every column written, with its value; greyed rows are filled later.
  • ERROR_CODE = DPS refuses and says why · ok = normal outcome.

Outside DPS. Built by the Spring team (thin Java wrappers over existing services). On the laptop Spring is not running. DPS never sees this call.

Read left to right; numbers give the order. Rows below the main path are the "if" routes. Code paths are under C:\cts-dps\dps\src\dps\.
  • Spring sends the file to the DMS store API. The DMS keeps one fixed copy and gives back its location (objectKey) and version ID.
  • Fingerprint (SHA-256): a 64-character code worked out from every byte of the file, for example cba19007448c...fecfa. Same content gives the same code, whatever the file name; one changed character gives a completely different code.
  • DPS uses the fingerprint three ways: the file's name in storage, proof the file was not changed (checked in 2.4 and 4.1), and spotting the same document sent twice (2.5).
  • The file is saved as <first 2 characters>\<fingerprint>.<extension>, for example cb\cba19007...fecfa.pdf. The 2-character folder only spreads files over folders. Already there (same content) → not written again.
  • Bank: the DMS folder is shared with DPS read-only (/dms/blobs). Laptop: the folder C:\cts-dps\dps\storage\ plays the DMS (setting DPS_STORAGE_DIR).
APIDMS store APISpring stores the file in the DMS · not a DPS APIDMS API · built by the DMS team
① Request · Spring → DMSthe file bytes
→
② DMS worksoutside DPS: the DMS keeps one fixed copy
→
③ Answer · DMS → Springobject key + version

Outside DPS. Built by the Spring and DMS team. DPS never calls it; DPS only reads the DMS folder, read-only.

What the DMS gives back is what Spring puts in the request's document part. For our file (on the laptop FileStore.put plays the DMS) REAL:

objectKey: cb/cba19007448c20a24d23faf7be48857f068363d9f93823c1cd9acb43ff7fecfa.pdf
sha256:    cba19007448c20a24d23faf7be48857f068363d9f93823c1cd9acb43ff7fecfa
versionId: v-cba19007448c
sizeBytes: 1734296

87 print(f"1. DMS stored {args.file.name} ({len(data) // 1024} KB) as {key}")prints step 1
dps/src/dps/ingest/file_store.pylines 14-22 · FileStore.put
14 def put(self, data: bytes, extension: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
15 """Stores bytes once per content hash. Returns (sha256, relative path)."""
16 digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()the fingerprint of every byte
17 rel = f"{digest[:2]}/{digest}{extension}"2 characters / fingerprint . extension
18 target = self.root / rel
19 if not target.exists():already there? then nothing is written
20 target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
21 target.write_bytes(data)the bytes, unchanged
22 return digest, relgives back the fingerprint and the key
deploy/docker-compose.cts-dps.ymllines 45-46 · bank: DPS sees the DMS folder
45 - ${DMS_BLOBS:-/srv/dms/blobs}:/dms/blobs:robank: the DMS folder, read-only for DPS
46 - ${DMS_STAGING:-/srv/dms/staging}:/dms/staging:rofiles not yet committed (ANALYZE)
Stored in the DMS: the original file, byte for byte, here only. DPS never changes it.

1.3Spring builds the job request (job request JSON · jobType)

  • The request has three parts: jobType (what to do), document (where the file is, from the DMS in 1.2) and context (CP, borrower, who uploaded). The whole request, field by field, opens step 2 (2.0).
  • jobType comes from the document type the RM chose in 1.1:
RM chose on the screenSpring sends jobType
aLet DPS decide / Loan agreementONBOARD (DPS finds the type, step 5.3)
bAmendment · WaiverEXTRACT_AMENDMENT · EXTRACT_WAIVER
cFinancial statement · Sanction letter · Compliance certificateEXTRACT_STATEMENT · EXTRACT_SANCTION · EXTRACT_CERTIFICATE
dnothing (Spring asks by itself)ANALYZE · RECONCILE_SET · DRAFT_COMMENTARY
  • DPS knows these job types from this dictionary; each sets the flow it runs in and the document type it expects. An unknown name is refused in 2.2.

How step 1 and step 2 fit together

Step 2 is not a new call. It is what DPS does inside the POST /dps/v1/jobs call that Spring sent at the end of step 1, while Spring waits for the answer. If a check fails, DPS answers with an error and saves nothing. The file itself is not read here.

  3. 2.7 builds the answer

Every check that says no stops the call at once: Spring gets an error answer and nothing is saved. Two checks can also stop early with a yes, already done: 3 (same request again) and 5 (same file again) return the existing job.

2.1Who is calling? (authentication and role check · require_roles) check 1 of 5

What DPS checksIs the caller Spring (role SERVICE) or an administrator?
In our run✓ X-Roles: SERVICE → allowed.
If not, Spring gets (nothing is saved)
  • no or wrong sign-in: 401 UNAUTHORIZED (from the code)
  • another role: 403 FORBIDDEN (from the code)

Like a guard checking a badge at the door, DPS first checks who sent the call.

Who sends the callAllowed?Why
The Spring app (signs in as SERVICE)✅ yesThe normal way: every upload from the CTS screen comes through Spring.
A DPS administrator: a person from the IT team (signs in as ADMIN)✅ yesRarely, by hand: a test upload, or resending a job after a fix.
Anyone else: an RM directly, support, an auditor❌ noThey may look at jobs, not create them.

The RM never calls DPS. The RM clicks Upload on the CTS screen; Spring calls DPS for them and writes the RM's name in the request (requestedBy), so DPS still knows who uploaded. Bank: the sign-in is a token from the bank's login system (Entra ID). Laptop: two headers stand in for it, X-User and X-Roles.

Code api\jobs.py:331 (require_roles): it is the first line of submit_job, whose code is shown with check 3

2.2Is the request filled in correctly? (schema validation · JobRequest) check 2 of 5

What DPS checksDoes the JSON have every required field, no unknown field, the right kinds of value?
In our run✓ the body of ① has the right shape → go on.
If not, Spring gets (nothing is saved)
  • unknown job type EXTRACT_GUARANTEE: 400 VALIDATION_FAILED REAL

DPS compares the JSON with the agreed format (the contract contracts\schemas\job-request.json): every required field is there, there is no unknown field, and each value is the right kind (a number where a number is expected, one of the known job types, a 64-character fingerprint ...). This runs before any DPS code (FastAPI does it). If something is wrong, the answer lists each wrong field in details.errors.

2.3Has Spring sent this exact request before? (idempotency · Idempotency-Key) check 3 of 5

What DPS checksIs the Idempotency-Key there, and was it used before?
In our run✓ upload-agr-0001 is new → go on.
If not, Spring gets (nothing is saved)
  • no key: 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED REAL
  • same key, different body: 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED REAL
  • same key, same body (a retry): 200 "duplicate": true REAL: the same job comes back

Spring puts a unique label on every request: the Idempotency-Key header (8 to 128 characters). Why: if the network breaks after DPS saved the job, Spring does not know it worked and sends again. The label lets DPS recognise the repeat, so one upload never becomes two jobs.

The keyDPS does
newgoes on to check 4
seen before, same bodyreturns the job it already made (200)
seen before, different bodyrefuses: 409 (a key may belong to one request only)
missingrefuses: 400

2.4Is the job allowed, and is the file really there? (business validation · validate_job) check 4 of 5

What DPS checksJob type available? File type allowed? Base covenants for a waiver? File really there, fingerprint the same?
In our run✓ ONBOARD, a PDF, found under the objectKey, SHA-256 matches → go on.
If not, Spring gets (nothing is saved)
  • waiver without the approved covenants: 400 BASE_REQUIRED REAL
  • file missing or too big: 400 INVALID_INPUT (from the code)
  • fingerprint differs: 400 INTEGRITY_MISMATCH (from the code)
  • queue full: 429 QUEUE_FULL (from the code)

The business rules of the request, one after another:

  • the job type is one DPS can do today;
  • the file type is allowed (PDF, Excel, CSV, Word; JSON only for a document set or commentary);
  • a waiver brings the approved covenants; an amendment brings them or the version it changes; a statement brings its period end;
  • the file is really in the DMS folder under objectKey, at most 50 MB;
  • DPS works out the fingerprint again from the stored file: it must equal the sha256 Spring sent (the file was not changed);
  • the queue for this bank is not full.

2.5Is this file already being read? (duplicate detection · input_key) check 5 of 5

What DPS checksIs there already a job for the same file and the same details?
In our run✓ no such job → a new job is made (2.6).

Different from check 3: this is a new request (a new key), but for the same file with the same details, for example the RM uploading the same agreement again. DPS builds a fingerprint of the job (job type, DPS version, file, its SHA-256, CP and the other details) and looks for a job with the same one. Found: the existing job comes back, so the file is not read twice. After a DPS upgrade the version differs, so the same file is read again as a new job.

2.8How Spring follows the job (job status and event feed)

  • Spring has three ways to know what is happening to the job; the three API cards below are them, in this order:
  • 1. Pull the notices (the main way): GET /dps/v1/events. DPS writes a notice for every change (accepted, done, needs review, failed); Spring asks for the new ones. Used again in step 12.
  • 2. Get the notices pushed (optional): DPS posts the same notices to Spring's POST /api/v1/dps-tools/events.
  • 3. Ask about one job: GET /dps/v1/jobs/{jobId} gives its status now. On the laptop, submit_job.py does this every 1.5 s (submit_job.py:116).
GET/dps/v1/eventsSpring asks for the new notices · read onlyDPS API · built by us (DPS)
① Request · Spring → DPSafter = last notice number
→
② Save · DPS → dps.dbnothing saved (read only)
→
③ Response · DPS → Spring200 · the notices after it

2Save — what DPS does in dps.db during the call

2.1 Order of work
#What DPS doesTables
aChecks: role, at most 500 files, one tenant, key not used before, queue not full; creates the batch · commitdps_batchdps_tenant_limitdps_job
bAGR-2020-001 is OK → a normal job (document, CP link, job, notice, audit line) · commitdps_documentdps_document_cp_linkdps_jobdps_audit_eventdps_event_feed
cAMD-2010-077 has the same input as an earlier job → recorded as DUPLICATE, not queued · commitdps_documentdps_job
dFS-2026-Q2 fails a check → recorded as REJECTED; the batch goes on · commitdps_documentdps_job
eAll files finished? No → the batch stays RUNNINGdps_batchdps_job

green new row · orange changed row · blue read only. Colours come from the SQL DPS really ran in this call.

One commit per file, so a bad file never undoes the others. dps_tenant_limit is only read: the default limit from the settings is used.

If CANCEL / RETRYin 2.8Spring can stop a job; support can restart one
  • Cancel: a waiting job ends CANCELLED at once; a running job is flagged and stops at its next check (3.5, 11.2). Already finished → 409 JOB_FINISHED.
  • Retry (support or admin only): a FAILED or DEAD job goes back to QUEUED with fresh attempts; else 409 JOB_NOT_RETRYABLE. Both are audited.
dps/src/dps/jobs.pylines 287-297 · request_cancel
287def request_cancel(db: Session, job: Job, user: str) -> Job:
288 """A waiting job is cancelled at once; a running one is flagged and stops at its next checkpoint."""
289 if job.status in FINAL:already finished: 409
290 raise JobFinished(job.status)
291 if job.status == RUNNING:running: flagged, stops at its next check
292 job.cancel_requested, job.updated_at = True, utcnow()
293 db.commit()
294 return job
295 job.cancel_requested = True
296 finish(db, job, CANCELLED, f"Cancelled by {user}", "JOB_CANCELLED", {"cancelledBy": user})waiting: CANCELLED now, event dps.job.cancelled
297 return job
dps/src/dps/api/jobs.pylines 436-444 · retry_failed_job

439 raise ApiError(409, "JOB_NOT_RETRYABLE", f"Job is {job.status}, not FAILED or DEAD")
440 now = utcnow()
441 job.status, job.attempts, job.error, job.error_code = jobs.QUEUED, 0, None, Noneback in the queue, attempts 0
442 job.crash_count, job.due_at, job.finished_at, job.updated_at = 0, now, None, now
443 job.cancel_requested = False
444 services.audit(db, user.user, "JOB_RETRY", "job", job.id)audited

The answer to POST /dps/v1/batches is only a receipt (the batch ID). Like a parcel tracking number, Spring uses that ID later to ask what happened to each file. Step 3 in plain words
Why this stepStep 2 only put the job on a waiting list and answered Spring at once. Reading a 100-page file takes about a minute: too long to keep Spring waiting. So the reading is done in the background, by a separate DPS program.
Who does itThe DPS worker: a DPS program that runs all the time, next to the API. It is not an API: nobody calls it. There can be several workers (bank: several containers; laptop: Terminal B).

What it writesOn our job's row: RUNNING, which worker has it and until when (the lock). Plus one new dps_job_attempt row: try number 1.

How it works

The worker runs in a loop. Every 2 seconds it asks dps.db: "is there a job waiting for me?" If not, it waits 2 seconds and asks again. Before asking, one of the workers (the leader, chosen automatically) also does the housekeeping for everyone: it pushes notices to Spring, moves old waiting jobs up, takes back jobs of workers that died, and seals the audit log once a day.

3.2Which waiting job goes first? (job queue · priority scheduling) 2 of 5

What DPS doesMost urgent first: priority, then due time, then age. A fair share per bank and per bulk upload.
In our runonly one job waiting: ours, priority 1 (INTERACTIVE, the highest)
If it goes wrongthe bank already has 4 running jobs → this one waits its turn
How it works

The worker does not take jobs in arrival order. It picks the most urgent: first the priority (an RM's own upload, INTERACTIVE, before a bulk import), then the time it may start, then age. To be fair, one bank may have at most 4 jobs running at once and one bulk upload at most 2, so a big import never blocks an RM's single upload. A job whose worker died (its lock ran out) can also be picked again.

3.3How does the worker take the job, so no other worker takes it too? (atomic claim · lease) 3 of 5

What DPS doesOne update that only works if the row is still exactly as read: status RUNNING, locked by this worker for 120 s, one more attempt.
In our runQUEUED → RUNNING, locked by dps-worker-1, attempt 1 at 02:59:57 UTC
If it goes wronganother worker was faster → 0 rows change, this worker tries the next job · died on it twice → DEAD (PARSER_CRASH)
How it works

Several workers may look at the same waiting job at the same moment. To make sure only one gets it, the worker changes the row with one database update that only works if the row is still exactly as it read it. The winner's update changes 1 row; a slower worker's changes 0 rows, and it simply tries the next job. The winner marks the job RUNNING, writes its own name and a time limit (now + 120 s, the lock), and opens a new attempt row. A job whose worker died on it twice is set aside as a poison file (DEAD) and never taken again.

3.4What if the worker stops halfway? (heartbeat · lease renewal · attempt fence) 4 of 5

What DPS doesWhile it works, the worker renews its lock every 40 s. Before every save it checks it still owns the job.
In our runthe job finished in under a minute, inside the first 120 s lock
If it goes wrongthe worker dies → the lock runs out → another worker takes the job (3.2) · a late worker may not save (LeaseLost)
How it works

The lock lasts 120 seconds. While the worker is busy, a small helper renews it every 40 seconds, like a heartbeat. If the worker crashes, the heartbeat stops, the lock runs out and another worker can take the job (3.2). Before saving anything, the worker checks it still holds the job; a worker that lost it may never overwrite the work of the one that took over.

What DPS doesThe job type decides the path: a document job goes to reading (step 4), then to its skill (step 5).

Step 4 in plain words
Is this extraction?No, not yet. Step 4 only turns the PDF into text, like typing out every page and noting where each line sits. Nothing is found or understood here. Finding the covenants and their values (the extraction) is steps 5-10.
What is the page model?The typed-out document: for each page, its lines of text and where each line is on the page (a box), plus its tables. Every later step reads this, never the PDF again. It is saved once as a file.
Why this stepA PDF is only bytes. To find covenants, DPS needs the words, and where each line is on its page (for the highlight box the reviewer sees later).
Who does itThe same worker, straight after step 3.
What it readsThe original file in the DMS folder (read-only), found with the objectKey of step 2.
What it writesThe text of every page (the page model) as one file in DPS's own folder, plus one dps_artifact row that lists it. The original file is never changed.
What Spring seesStill RUNNING.
Where the code isC:\cts-dps\dps\src\dps\ + ingest\ (store.py, pipeline.py, inspect.py) · parse\ (sandbox.py, engine.py, page_model.py, segment.py)
How step 3 and step 4 fit together

Same worker, same job, no new call. Right after claiming the job (step 3), the worker reads the file itself from the DMS folder (read-only). It does not call the DMS API.

How it works

The worker reads the original file from the DMS folder and, while reading, works out its fingerprint again. It must equal the fingerprint Spring sent in step 1: then the file is exactly the one that was uploaded. If not, someone changed it after upload: the job fails and support is alerted.

4.3Is the file safe to open? (file inspection · type spoofing) 3 of 7

What DPS doesChecks the first bytes match the type and looks for passwords, JavaScript, embedded files, macros, zip bombs.
In our runa real PDF (starts with %PDF-), nothing unsafe ✓

How it works

Before opening the file, DPS checks it is safe: the first bytes must really be a PDF, and it must not have a password, JavaScript, embedded files or (for Office files) macros or a zip bomb. A dangerous file is refused and the DMS is asked to put it in quarantine.

4.4How is it opened without risk? (sandbox · child process) 4 of 7

What DPS doesOpens the file in a separate child program with no network, a memory limit and a time limit.
In our runopened in the STANDARD pool (2 GB, at most 15 min) ✓
If it goes wrongtoo slow or too big → moved to the HEAVY pool · the child crashes → retried once
How it works

The file is opened in a locked box: a separate small program with no network, a memory limit and a time limit. If a broken or harmful file makes it crash, only that small program dies, never the worker. A file that needs more time or memory (e.g. a big scan) is moved to the HEAVY workers.

Each page becomes text. For a normal PDF the words are taken from the PDF itself; only a page that is a picture is read with OCR (text recognition, on this computer, nothing leaves it). 4.7What if reading fails? (failure handling · HEAVY pool) 7 of 7

What DPS doesDecides: try again in the HEAVY pool, retry later, or fail with a reason.
In our runnothing failed
If it goes wrongtoo slow → HEAVY pool · parser crash or storage down → retried (Extra A) · anything else → FAILED with its code
How it works

If reading is too slow or needs too much memory, the job moves to the HEAVY workers. A crash of the locked box or a storage problem is tried again later. Anything else ends the job FAILED, with the reason.

Step 5 in plain words
Is this extraction?Yes, it starts here. First DPS decides what the document is, then which skill (the reader for that kind of document) will do the extraction in steps 6-10.
What is a skill?A skill pack is one folder per kind of document, e.g. skills\covenants\. It holds: the rules (rules.py, Python, no AI), the AI task (prompt.md), the AI answer format (schema.json) and its settings (pack.yaml: page limits, which tools the AI may use).
Why this stepSpring sent ONBOARD: "let DPS decide". A loan agreement, an amendment or a sanction letter each need a different reader, so DPS first finds out what the document is.
Who does itThe same worker. From here to step 11 the work runs inside one CrewAI flow (a fixed sequence of steps).
What it readsThe first pages from memory; with AI on, the bank's Azure for a second opinion; Spring, to match the IDs found.
What it writesOnly a progress mark on the job (current_step = START). The decision itself stays in memory until step 11.
What Spring seesRUNNING, current step START.

From here to step 11 the job runs as one CrewAI flow: a fixed sequence with two parts, "run the skills" (steps 5-10) and "save the result" (step 11). CrewAI is the framework DPS uses to run its AI agent; the flow itself makes no AI call. When AI is off, everything runs with the rules only.

How it works

Only for ONBOARD ("let DPS decide"). The rules look at the first pages: title words, phrases, numbers, and give each document type a score. A clear winner decides. With AI on, the AI gives a second opinion with quotes; if it disagrees, a person decides. If the type found differs from what the RM chose, a person checks it too.

How it works

Step 6 begins the extraction run of the chosen skill (runner.run). It is the setup for both readers: it reads the job's context from dps_job.request_json (the CP, the borrower and, for an amendment or a waiver, the approved covenants), and when AI is on it opens the job's token budget (700,000 for the covenants pack, from pack.yaml). That budget is only spent by the AI in step 8; the rules in 6.3 run on this computer and cost nothing. Then the run goes to the right reader: a statement, a document set or a commentary has its own reader; every other pack goes to _extract, where the rules run first (6.3) and the AI after them (steps 7-8).

6.2Rules (no AI)Amendment or waiver only: load the covenants it changes (base covenants) 2 of 4

What DPS doesAn amendment or a waiver changes covenants that were already approved. Before reading it, DPS loads those approved covenants (the base), so it can say what changed.
In our runour document is a loan agreement, not an amendment or a waiver → this sub-step is skipped
If it goes wrongno base found → BASE_UNKNOWN: every change goes to a person
How it works

Only for an amendment or a waiver. Such a letter only makes sense next to what was approved before. Example: the letter says "in clause 21.2, 1.20 is replaced by 1.10". On its own that says nothing about which covenant. With the base (AC-11: DSCR ≥ 1.20, clause 21.2) DPS can say: DSCR changed from ≥ 1.20 to ≥ 1.10. The base comes from Spring (context.baseCovenants, preferred: covenants people approved) or, if Spring did not send it, from DPS's own earlier reading of the agreement (amendsVersionId; flagged BASE_FROM_DPS).

A real misreading: the rules read Icr · ICR < 0.75 on page 9, but that sentence is about a benchmark interest-rate floor (0.75 %), not a covenant. The AI did not confirm it. This is why every covenant goes to a person (step 13): the reviewer rejects it.

How do the rules know what to look for? (no AI, no learning)

The rules are Python code with fixed lists and text patterns, written by developers. They do not learn and they do not read the taxonomy. The files are under C:\cts-dps\dps\src\dps\.

What the rules knowWhere it is writtenWhat it holds

How it works

The rules read every page: numbered clauses, covenant names ("Interest Coverage Ratio"), the test ("not less than 2.50" becomes >= 2.5), how often it is tested, step-downs and cures, each with its page and exact quote. A sentence that looks like a covenant but no rule understood is never dropped: it is kept as POSSIBLE_COVENANT for a person.

Coordinates: where the page, quote and box of each finding come from, and where they are kept REAL

Neither the rules nor the AI measure positions. They give a page and an exact quote; DPS then finds that line in the page model, which already knows the box of every line, and copies its box (bbox) and line id (blockId) into the field. bbox = [left, top, right, bottom] in PDF points (1/72 inch), measured from the top-left corner of the page (a US-letter page is 612 × 792). For Excel and CSV there is no box but a cell (cellRef, e.g. B4).

Other paths in this step

The main path above is a loan agreement sent alone. These boxes say what changes for the other kinds of upload; each one names the sub-step it belongs to.

If STATEMENTin 6.1its own reader, not the field rules
  • The statement reader (skills\statement_lines\reader.py) reads the file: the table reader for PDFs (OCR quality, periods, last year's column), rows for XLSX, XLS and CSV.
  • It uses the borrower's label memory, Spring's loan currency, FX rate and borrower profile, and checks the units, the period and the entity against the assessment cycle.
  • Too many pages it cannot read → moved to the HEAVY pool; no lines at all → FAILED CONTENT_FAILED.
  • Every figure is a STATEMENT_LINE field; a statement is never reported without review.

WarningMeaning (error catalogue)
CURRENCY_DIFFERSThe statement's currency differs from the loan's; figures were converted, please confirm.
CURRENCY_MIXEDThe statement shows amounts in more than one currency; please confirm which applies.
LOAN_CURRENCY_UNKNOWNThe loan's currency is not known; set it in the borrower's settings.
LOANS_DIFFERThe borrower's loans are in different currencies; please confirm the currency used.
INTEREST_IS_NETInterest is shown net of income; the covenant may need gross interest.
LOW_OCR_QUALITYScanned pages were read with low OCR confidence; please check the figures.
NUMBER_STYLE_UNCLEARThe statement writes numbers in two styles; please confirm the decimal separator.
MISSING_LINE_ITEMSLines the covenants need (EBITDA, total debt, net worth) were not found.
LABEL_MEMORY_CONFLICTA line was confirmed earlier as another item for this borrower; please check which is right.
SECOND_READER_DIFFERSThe AI checker read another figure than the rules; please check the source.
SECOND_READER_EMPTYThe AI checker read none of the figures; the statement waits for a person.
DEBT_DOES_NOT_ADD_UPShort-term and long-term debt do not add up to total debt.
NEGATIVE_VALUEA figure that cannot be negative was read as negative; please check its sign.
AMOUNT_SCALE_UNCLEARNo scale (thousand, lakh, crore, million) is stated for the amount; please confirm it.
UNIT_NOT_STATEDThe statement does not state its unit; amounts were read in the default unit, please confirm.
LINES_NOT_FOUNDStatement lines the reader did not find; listed so none is missing silently.
If AMENDMENTin 6.3rules find each change against the base
  • Per covenant: ADD, CHANGE or DELETE, with the clause ("Clause 18.2 shall stand amended ..."), the effective date and the old test (from).
  • A clause restated unchanged is not a change. No unique approved target → AMBIGUOUS_AMENDMENT_TARGET; unclear → UNRESOLVED_AMENDMENT; changed twice → CHANGED_TWICE.
  • Base from DPS's own earlier reading → BASE_FROM_DPS; no base found → BASE_UNKNOWN (always reviewed). The schedule-terms rules also run (as for agreements).

Why a page was chosen: RULES SECTION DUTY DEFINITIONS. RULES = the rules found something there (6.3); SECTION = a covenant heading or the page after it; DUTY = sentences like "shall", "will not", most first; DEFINITIONS = the two best definition pages. Pages fill the first batch with room, so a batch is not in one page range. In our run every part found its words in every batch, so all 4 parts read all 6 batches.

How it works

The AI gets only the pages that matter, in this order: pages the rules used, covenant headings and the page after, pages with duty sentences, the best definition pages. At most 25 pages per batch, at most 12 batches. Pages that fit nowhere are listed; the AI can still open them with its tools.

How does the AI know what to look for?

Everything the AI knows about covenants is sent in each message: the task, the bank's list of covenant kinds (the taxonomy) and the answer format. So the AI answers with the bank's codes; the rules' findings get the same codes in step 10.1, and step 9 can compare the two.

What the AI is givenWhere it comes fromWhat it holds
The taskskills\covenants\prompt.md"Find {scope} in these pages of a loan agreement … Give each item a code from the bank's covenant taxonomy below … Never make up a code. One item per duty."
The list of covenant kindsskills\covenants\taxonomy\default_taxonomy.yaml (the bank's 92 kinds) + dps_overlay.yamleach kind: code, category, name, description, aliases, keywords. Each of the 4 parts gets only its categories in its prompt (parts.py): financial · affirmative + negative · reporting · events of default
The answer formatskills\covenants\schema.jsona list of items: name, page, quote, value
The pagesstep 7.1only the pages that matter, whole pages, in batches
Tools to look furtherpack.yaml → toolspage_text, search_text, find_definition (DPS); covenant_library, validate_formula (Spring)
The modelthe bank's Azure OpenAI (azure/gpt-6.1-sol)a general pre-trained model; not trained on our documents; a fresh agent each read, no memory between jobs
How it works

Covenants are read in four focused parts: financial, undertakings, reporting and events of default. Each part has its own short list of the bank's covenant types. All parts get the same pages first, so the bank's AI service can re-use them and charges less.

112def fit_pages(pages: list[dict], limit: int = MAX_PROMPT_CHARS) -> tuple[str, list[int]]:
113 """The page blocks that fit in ``limit`` characters, whole pages only, and the pages left out. A page is never
114 cut in the middle: the agent would read half a clause and nobody would know (19 Nov 2026 review)."""
115 blocks, left_out, used = [], [], 0
116 for p in pages:
117 block = f"<<<page {p[&#x27;no']}>>>\n{p.get('text') or ''}\n<<<end page {p['no']}>>>"each page between markers
118 if used + len(block) + 1 > limit:does not fit: left out whole
119 left_out.append(p["no"])
120 continue
121 blocks.append(block)
122 used += len(block) + 1
123 return "\n".join(blocks), left_out

126def prompt_for(pack, pages: list[dict], extra: str = "", notes: list | None = None) -> list[dict]:
127 from dps.agent.guard import DATA_NOT_INSTRUCTIONS

133 "can still open them)"))

135 # tasks (the four covenant parts) share a long identical prefix, which Azure's prompt cache serves at a discount
136 # (full review G32). The task, schema and batch note follow the pages.
137 content = "\n\n".join([HEADER.format(guard=DATA_NOT_INSTRUCTIONS), blocks, "Task:\n" + pack.prompt.strip(),header, pages, task, schema, batch note
138 "Schema:\n" + json.dumps(pack.schema), extra])
139 return [{"role": "user", "content": content}]one message

Extraction by AI, part 2: the AI reads

The bank's AI proposes values, each with its page and exact quote

Trace (OpenTelemetry → Langfuse, new 23 Nov 2026): one span dps.ai.read covenants per batch (part i of n, pages, first and last page, proposals, notes) and under it one span chat azure/<deployment> per model call: model, tokens in and out, prompt version, attempt. A retried call is its own red span. Prompt and answer text only with DPS_AI_TRACE_TEXT=true, masked. The dps_ai_call row of each call now has the same trace_id and span_id. Code agent/gateway.py Gateway.call, skills/common.py batched_proposals.
Whothe worker: skills/common.py:145 agent_proposals, agent/document_agent.py, agent/gateway.py
Inputthe prompt (step 7) and the whole page model (for the tools)
Outputthe AI's proposals: name, value, page, quote (in memory); every call recorded in dps.db
Main path (step 8): AGREEMENT loan agreement, ONBOARD / EXTRACT_AGREEMENT · Other paths in this step: STATEMENT SET (each in its "If" box)
Step 8 in plain words
Is this extraction?Yes: extraction by AI, only when AI is on. The Document Agent (a CrewAI AI agent using the bank's Azure model) reads the pages and proposes values, each with page and quote.
What are its tools?Small DPS functions the agent may call while it reads: page_text (open a page), search_text (find words), find_definition (look up a defined term), covenant_library and validate_formula (ask Spring). Listed in the skill's pack.yaml.
Why this stepRules miss unusual wording. The AI reads like a person, but must show the exact quote and page for everything it proposes, so it can be checked.
Who does itThe same worker, through DPS's gateway, calling the bank's own Azure OpenAI. Only when AI is on.
What it readsThe prompt of step 7; the AI may also open other pages with its tools.
What it writesOne dps_ai_call row per call and one dps_ai_usage row per job (costs, tokens).

Coordinates: the AI gives a page and a quote only; after the quote check, DPS takes the box from the page model and saves it with the field in dps_run.result_json (see 6.4).

How it works

The AI proposes values, each with a quote. Every quote must really be on the page it names. If one is not, the AI is asked once to correct it; still wrong, that item is dropped. If the AI is down or the budget is spent, the rules' answers stand and a warning says so.

8.2AI onlyWho asks the AI? (Document Agent · CrewAI Agent) 2 of 7

What DPS doesA fresh CrewAI agent per read, with only the skill's tools. It proposes; it never decides.

How it works

The Document Agent is a fresh CrewAI agent for each read, with no memory and only the skill's tools (open a page, search the text, find a definition, ask Spring's covenant library or formula check). Its job: propose each value with page and quote. It never decides.

8.3AI onlyWhat protects the calls? (AI gateway) 3 of 7

What DPS doesOne gateway for every AI call: budget, retries, circuit breaker, rate limit.
In our run30 of 30 calls OK, no retry needed; budget not exceeded (the re-read was cut by its own budget: RESIDUAL_BUDGET)
If it goes wrongbudget spent → AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
How it works

Every AI call of DPS goes through one gateway: it picks the model, counts the job's budget, stops calling a model that keeps failing, respects a rate limit and retries after 2, 8 and 30 seconds.

How it works

Before any text leaves DPS, personal data (e-mail, phone, PAN, Aadhaar, IBAN, card numbers) is masked. The same question to the same model is answered from a cache and not paid twice. The monthly budget is checked before each call.

How it works

For every AI proposal, DPS looks for the quote on its page (ignoring line breaks; the page before or after also counts). Not found means the AI could not show it, so it is dropped.

Code skills/common.py:53 (grounded)
dps/src/dps/skills/common.pylines 53-69 · grounded
53def grounded(pages: list[dict], page_no: int | None, quote: str | None) -> bool:
54 """The quote is on the cited page, on the page just before or after it (a page number one off), or runs across
55 the break between the cited page and a neighbour. Line breaks and hyphenated line ends are ignored."""
56 q = _flat(quote)no line breaks, no hyphenation
57 page = page_of(pages, page_no)
58 if page is None or len(q) < 4:no page or no real quote: not grounded
59 return False
60 here = _flat(page.get("text"))
61 if q in here:on the page itself
62 return True
63 before, after = page_of(pages, (page_no or 0) - 1), page_of(pages, (page_no or 0) + 1)
64 for other in (before, after):or on the page before / after
65 if other is not None and q in _flat(other.get("text")):
66 return True
67 if after is not None and q in f"{here} {_flat(after.get(&#x27;text'))}":or across the page break
68 return True
69 return before is not None and q in f"{_flat(before.get(&#x27;text'))} {here}"

9.2Rules + AIDo the rules and the AI agree? (vote · consensus) 2 of 4

What DPS doesSame covenant, same test → confirmed by both (confidence at least 0.95); different → a person decides.
In our run7 values found by both rules and AI with the same test: confirmed by both
If it goes wrongthey differ → MODELS_DISAGREE, a person decides
How it works

The rules' finding and the AI's finding for the same covenant are put side by side. Same test and value: confirmed by both, high confidence. Different: both values go to a person, who decides.

9.4Rules + AIWas any duty sentence missed? (coverage ledger) 4 of 4

What DPS doesLists every covenant-shaped sentence of the whole document and gives each an outcome.
In our run171 duty sentences, 156 explained (91.2%); 4 found in the AI's re-read; the rest go to a person
If it goes wronggaps → COVERAGE_GAP with the pages
How it works

The ledger makes sure nothing is missed: it lists every sentence of the whole document that sounds like a duty ("shall", "will not", "not less than" ...) and gives each one an outcome: found, covered, not a covenant (with a reason), or open. Every open sentence goes to a person.

10.4Rules + AIHow sure is DPS? Person or auto? (confidence scoring · routing) 4 of 5

What DPS doesStarts at 0.97 and subtracts for each weakness; high-risk fields (every covenant) always go to a person.
In our run158 of 158 fields need a person (every covenant is high risk)
If it goes wrong—
How it works

Each field gets a confidence: it starts at 0.97 and loses points for each weakness (no quote, readers disagree, a failed check, poor text ...). Then the route: high-risk fields (every covenant) always go to a person; others are accepted when confident enough. A small sample of the accepted ones is checked by a person anyway.

70 ("grounded", lambda s: s["grounded"] < 1, 0.45),no page/quote

91 value += bonus

95 return Score(round(min(0.99, max(0.05, value)), 3), [r for _, r in hits[:3]], "RULE_TABLE")kept between 0.05 and 0.99

Inputthe result built in steps 5-10
Outputdps_run (THE EXTRACTION), dps_job NEEDS_REVIEW or DONE, the event
Main path (step 11): AGREEMENT loan agreement, ONBOARD / EXTRACT_AGREEMENT · Other paths in this step: ANALYZE AMENDMENT SET COMMENTARY BULK CANCEL / RETRY (each in its "If" box)
Step 11 in plain words
Why this stepEverything found is kept as one document that never changes, and Spring is told the job has finished.
Who does itThe same worker: the last thing it does for this job. Then it is free for the next one.
What it readsThe finished result in memory.
What it writesIn one go: the result (dps_run, run 1), the job's end status (NEEDS_REVIEW or DONE), the attempt closed, and a notice for Spring (dps_event_feed).
What Spring seesA new notice: dps.extraction.needs_review. The status is now NEEDS_REVIEW.

11.2How is it saved, and the job ended? (save run · finish job · event) 2 of 2

What DPS doesOne commit: the run, the job's end status, the attempt closed, the notice for Spring.
In our runrun 1 at 03:16:32 UTC; job NEEDS_REVIEW; notice no. 2 dps.extraction.needs_review
If it goes wrongthe worker lost the job meanwhile → it may not save (LeaseLost)
After step 11: everything this job left behind REAL
WhatWhereSize or count
the extraction (run 1)dps.db dps_run.result_json363,052 characters
the page modelfile page-model.json.gz + dps_artifact142,072 bytes
the AI callsdps.db dps_ai_call (+ 1 dps_ai_usage)30 rows
the job, its attempt, the notice, the audit linesdps.db dps_job, dps_job_attempt, dps_event_feed, dps_audit_event1 row each per change
a file of the resultnone: written only when you add --json to scripts\submit_job.py—
How it works

In one go: the result is saved as run 1 (never changed later; a review adds run 2), the job gets its end status, the attempt is closed and a notice for Spring is written. Either all of it is saved, or none: there is never a result without its notice.

145def amended_set(base: list[dict], changes: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
146 """The covenants as amended: base minus deletions, changed ones replaced, additions appended."""
147 result = [dict(f) for f in base if f["group"].endswith("COVENANT")]
148 for c in changes:
149 if any(i["code"] in ("AMBIGUOUS_AMENDMENT_TARGET", "UNRESOLVED_AMENDMENT", "CHANGED_TWICE")unclear changes are not applied
150 for i in c.get("issues", [])):
151 continue
152 value = c["value"]
153 change = value["change"]
154 if change["type"] == "ADD":added
155 result.append(c)
156 continue
157 target = change.get("appliedCovenantId")
158 if target:
159 positions = [i for i, f in enumerate(result)
160 if target in (f["value"].get("appliedCovenantId"),
161 (f["value"].get("change") or {}).get("appliedCovenantId"))]
162 else:
163 positions = [i for i, f in enumerate(result) if f["value"].get("metric") == value.get("metric")]
164 if len(positions) == 1:
165 if change["type"] == "DELETE":
166 result.pop(positions[0])deleted
167 else:
168 result[positions[0]] = cchanged: replaced

353def _sync_batch(db: Session, job: Job) -> None:
354 """When the last item of a batch ends, the batch completes and says so on the feed."""
355 if not job.batch_id:
356 return
357 db.flush()
358 open_items = db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Job)items still waiting or running
359 .where(Job.batch_id == job.batch_id, Job.status.not_in(FINAL + (NEEDS_REVIEW,))))
360 batch = db.get(Batch, job.batch_id)

362 return
363 batch.status, batch.finished_at = "COMPLETED", utcnow()batch done

367 counts[outcome] = counts.get(outcome, 0) + 1
368 failed = any(k in counts for k in ("REJECTED", "FAILED_RETRYABLE"))
369 feed.emit(db, "dps.batch.completed", tenant_id=batch.tenant_id, payload={event with counts
370 "batchId": batch.id, "counts": counts,

How it works

Spring asks DPS for new notices with GET /dps/v1/events, remembering the last number it saw. (Optionally DPS can also push the same notices to Spring.) The notice says the job is finished and where the result is.

12.2How does Spring get the result? (result API · ETag) 2 of 2

What DPS doesGET /dps/v1/jobs/{jobId}/result gives the saved result, with an ETag.
In our run200 with the result; asked again unchanged → 304
If it goes wrongnot finished → 404 RESULT_NOT_READY · cancelled → 410
How it works

Spring then fetches the result with GET /dps/v1/jobs/{jobId}/result: exactly the JSON saved in step 11. If nothing changed since last time, the answer is a short "not modified".

Code api/jobs.py:368 (job_result) · results.py:42 (build)
dps/src/dps/api/jobs.pylines 368-385 · GET /result
368@router.get("/dps/v1/jobs/{job_id}/result")
369def job_result(job_id: str, request: Request, db: DB, user: User) -> Response:
370 require_roles(user, SERVICE, ADMIN, SUPPORT)Spring, admin or support
371 job = _job_or_404(db, job_id)
372 if job.status == jobs.CANCELLED:
373 raise ApiError(410, "JOB_CANCELLED", "The job was cancelled.")410
374 if job.status not in (jobs.DONE, jobs.NEEDS_REVIEW):
375 raise ApiError(404, "RESULT_NOT_READY", f"The job is {job.status}.", {"status": job.status})404 while QUEUED / RUNNING
376 settings = _settings(request)
377 from dps.ingest.store import LocalStore
378
379 derived = LocalStore(settings.storage_dir, settings.staging_dir, settings.derived_dir)
380 body = results.build(db, job, settings.pipeline_version, derived)the latest dps_run.result_json
381 raw = json.dumps(body, default=str, separators=(",", ":"))
382 etag = &#x27;"' + hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:32] + '"'fingerprint of the answer
383 if request.headers.get("If-None-Match") == etag:
384 return Response(status_code=304, headers={"ETag": etag})unchanged since last time
385 return Response(raw, media_type="application/json", headers={"ETag": etag})

Step 13 in plain words
Why this stepDPS never approves anything. A person confirms, corrects or rejects what DPS proposed.
Who does itA reviewer on the CTS screen; Spring calls the DPS review API for them.
What it readsThe latest run of the job: only the fields that need a person, with their evidence.
What it writesEach decision, a new run with the changes (run 2), and possible test cases. The job becomes DONE when nothing is left to check.
What Spring seesThe reviewed result; when finished, the notice dps.extraction.completed.
Where the code isC:\cts-dps\dps\src\dps\ + api\review.py · api\evidence.py

How it works

The reviewer sees only the fields that need a person: DPS's value, both readers' values when they disagree, the confidence, the reasons, and the evidence (page, quote, box, page picture). The revision number makes sure two reviewers do not overwrite each other.

Code api/review.py:67 (GET review)
dps/src/dps/api/review.pylines 73-90 · GET review
73 result, revision = _current(db, job, request)the latest run and its number
74 version = job.document_version_id
75 fields = []
76 for f in result.get("fields", []):
77 if f.get("status") != "NEEDS_REVIEW":
78 continue
79 src = f.get("source") or {}
80 reasons = list((f.get("signals") or {}).get("reasons") or []) + [i["code"] for i in f.get("issues", [])]scorer reasons + issue codes
81 fields.append({
82 "fieldId": f["id"], "group": f["group"], "name": f["name"], "proposed": f["value"],the value DPS proposes
83 "readers": _readers(f) or {}, "confidence": f.get("confidence"),rules vs AI when they disagree
84 "reasons": list(dict.fromkeys(reasons)),
85 "evidence": {"page": src.get("page"), "quote": src.get("quote"), "bbox": src.get("bbox"),page, quote, box
86 "cellRef": src.get("cellRef"),
87 "pageImage": (f"/dps/v1/versions/{version}/pages/{src[&#x27;page']}/image"the page as a picture
88 if version and src.get("page") else None)}})
89 return {"jobId": job.id, "runId": result.get("runId", job.id), "revision": revision, "fields": fields,send it back as If-Match
90 "counts": {"toReview": len(fields), "total": len(result.get("fields", []))}}

13.2What does the reviewer send? (review decisions) 2 of 4

What DPS doesCONFIRM, CORRECT, REJECT, ADD or ACKNOWLEDGE, with the revision they loaded.
In our runone CONFIRM and one REJECT
If it goes wrongsomeone saved in between → 409 REVISION_CHANGED, reload
How it works

For each field the reviewer sends one decision: CONFIRM (right), CORRECT (new value and why), REJECT (not a covenant), ADD (something DPS missed) or ACKNOWLEDGE (a warning that does not block).

Code api/review.py:93-109 (Decision, Decisions)

95 fieldId: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64) # noqa: N815
96 # ACKNOWLEDGE: fieldId is "warning:<CODE>" and comment says why the warning does not block (full review G29)
97 action: Literal["CONFIRM", "CORRECT", "REJECT", "ADD", "ACKNOWLEDGE"]the five actions
98 group: str | None = None
99 name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
100 value: object | None = None

102 reasonCode: Literal["WRONG_VALUE", "WRONG_UNIT", "WRONG_PAGE", "NOT_A_COVENANT", "MISSED", # noqa: N815why it was corrected
103 "OTHER"] | None = None

13.3What does DPS save? (apply decisions · new run · golden set) 3 of 4

What DPS doesEach decision, a new run with the changes, the old run marked replaced; DONE when nothing is left.
In our run2 decisions, run 2, 1 golden-set candidate; the job stays NEEDS_REVIEW (fields left)
If it goes wrong—
How it works

DPS saves each decision with the old and new value, saves the changed result as a new run (run 2; run 1 is kept and marked as replaced), and keeps corrections as possible test cases. When nothing is left to check, the job becomes DONE and Spring gets a notice.

If RECLASSIFYin 13.2the type was wrong: a new job with the right pack
  • The reviewer sends the right type and a reason. DPS copies the old request, sets the new job type (e.g. SANCTION_LETTER → EXTRACT_SANCTION) and queues a new job (priority INTERACTIVE). It starts again at step 3; the file is not uploaded again.
  • The old job's runs get superseded_by = the new job; event dps.job.accepted with reclassifiedFrom; audited.

Read left to right; numbers give the order. Rows below the main path are the "if" routes. Code paths are under C:\cts-dps\dps\src\dps\.
How it works

Spring takes the confirmed and corrected fields, stores them as approved covenants in its own database, and decides compliance with its own Java rules and the statement figures. Later amendments and waivers send these approved covenants back to DPS (step 6.2).

DPS never approves a covenant and never decides compliance. It reads, proposes, shows its evidence and records what people decided.

Extra A · When a job fails

Retry, a bigger pool, FAILED or DEAD: what happens and what is stored

What happenedCodeWhat DPS doesJob ends
Spring or storage not reachableSPRING_UNAVAILABLE, STORAGE_UNAVAILABLEretry after ~10 s, then ~40 s; 3 attempts in allRETRY_WAIT, then DEAD
A bug while readingINTERNAL_ERRORretried onceDEAD on the second
The parser process crashedPARSER_CRASHretried onceDEAD on the second
The worker itself died twice on the filePARSER_CRASHpoison file: never claimed again (3.3)DEAD
Parsing too slow / out of memoryPARSE_TIMEOUT, OUT_OF_MEMORYmoved to the HEAVY pool (4.7)runs again there
The file is refusedTYPE_SPOOFED, UNSAFE_CONTENT, MACRO_PRESENT, ENCRYPTEDno retry; the DMS is asked to quarantine itFAILED
The file changed / is brokenINTEGRITY_MISMATCH, CORRUPT, TOO_MANY_PAGESno retryFAILED
No readable lines (statement)CONTENT_FAILEDno retryFAILED
CancelledJOB_CANCELLEDbefore start: stops; while running: result not publishedCANCELLED

A.1Retry later

  • Wait = min(15 min, 10 s × 4attempt-1) ±20%: about 10 s after attempt 1, 40 s after attempt 2 (3 attempts by default).
  • Attempts used up → DEAD, event dps.job.dead with the attempts.
  • Spring can start it again with POST /dps/v1/jobs/{jobId}/retry (contract line 133).
Code jobs.py:256 (retry_delay) · jobs.py:262 (release_for_retry)
dps/src/dps/jobs.pylines 256-274 · retry
256def retry_delay(attempt: int, base: float, maximum: float) -> float:
257 """``min(maximum, base * 4^(attempt-1))`` seconds, +/-20% so retries of one outage spread out."""
258 delay = min(maximum, base * (4 ** max(0, attempt - 1)))10 s × 4^(attempt-1), at most 15 min
259 return delay * random.uniform(0.8, 1.2) # retry jitter, not security # noqa: S311 # nosec B311±20%
260
261
262def release_for_retry(db: Session, job: Job, error: str, max_attempts: int, error_code: str = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
263 base_seconds: float = 10.0, max_seconds: float = 900.0) -> None:
264 """Transient failure: RETRY_WAIT until ``due_at``; when attempts run out, DEAD (ops alerted)."""
265 if job.attempts >= max_attempts:no attempts left ...
266 finish(db, job, DEAD, error, error_code)... DEAD, ops alerted by the event
267 return
268 guard_attempt(db)
269 now = utcnow()
270 job.status, job.error, job.error_code = RETRY_WAIT, error, error_codeelse wait
271 job.locked_by, job.locked_until, job.updated_at = None, None, now
272 job.due_at = now + timedelta(seconds=retry_delay(job.attempts, base_seconds, max_seconds))not claimed before this time (3.2)
273 _close_attempt(db, job, RETRY_WAIT, error_code)this attempt ends RETRY_WAIT
274 db.commit()

A.2Poison file

  • A file whose worker died twice (the lease ran out twice) is set aside: never claimed again.

dps/src/dps/jobs.pylines 143-159 · _bury_poison
143def _bury_poison(db: Session, job: Job, crashes: int) -> None:
144 """A file that killed its worker ``crashes`` times: DEAD, never claimed again, ops alerted by the event."""
145 now = utcnow()
146 result = db.execute(
147 update(Job)
148 .where(Job.id == job.id, Job.status == RUNNING, Job.attempts == job.attempts)
149 .values(status=DEAD, crash_count=crashes, error_code="PARSER_CRASH", locked_by=None, locked_until=None,DEAD, PARSER_CRASH
150 error="The worker stopped while processing this file, twice; it was set aside.",
151 finished_at=now, updated_at=now)
152 .execution_options(synchronize_session=False))
153 if result.rowcount == 1:
154 db.refresh(job)
155 _close_attempt(db, job, DEAD, "PARSER_CRASH")attempt closed
156 feed.emit_for_job(db, "dps.job.dead", job,event for operations
157 {"errorCode": "PARSER_CRASH", "message": job.error, "attempts": job.attempts})
158 _sync_batch(db, job)
159 db.commit()
Stored in dps.db: dps_job, the closed dps_job_attempt (outcome, error_code), dps_event_feed (dps.job.failed / dps.job.dead / dps.job.cancelled, payload errorCode and message), dps_document.status FAILED. Spring sees it with GET /dps/v1/jobs/{jobId} or the event.

B

Reference · security

Who may call what, and how DPS knows who is calling

B.2.1Sign-in

  • Bank (production): Entra ID JWT (DPS_AUTH_MODE=JWT, needs DPS_JWT_ISSUER and DPS_JWT_AUDIENCE); the token's roles decide what the caller may do.
  • Service-to-service: a service token (SERVICE_TOKEN mode), stored as its SHA-256 only.
  • Laptop: trusted headers X-User and X-Roles (DEV_HEADER), refused when DPS_ENV=prod. X-User only names the acting person; it never grants rights.

missing / wrong401 UNAUTHORIZED / 403 FORBIDDEN

B.2.3Tenants and data

  • Every job, batch, event and artefact carries tenant_id; a caller only sees its own tenant (same_tenant), else 404 / 403 TENANT_MISMATCH.
  • The AI only gets masked text (8.4) and only goes to hosts on DPS_AI_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
  • The parser has no network (4.4); containers run non-root with a read-only file system (Part C).

C.2Install on the laptop

  • One command: C:\cts-dps\dps\scripts\setup.ps1. Then the master script's commands (docs\cts-dps\demo\DPS-demo-master-script.pdf).
dps/scripts/setup.ps1lines 1-10 · setup.ps1
1# One-command local install of the CTS DPS on a Windows laptop (PowerShell 5.1 or 7).
2#
3# cd C:\cts-dps\dps
4# powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\setup.ps1 # install + smoke demoinstall + one-document demo
5# powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\setup.ps1 -Tests # also run the full test suitealso the full test suite
6# powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\setup.ps1 -Samples # also re-download the architect's demo files
7#
8# What it does, in order: checks Python (3.12 preferred, 3.11-3.13 accepted), creates .venv, installs the package withPython, venv, packages ...
9# the worker and dev extras, creates .env from .env.example (only if .env is missing), creates the SQLite tables with.env only if missing; tables via Alembic
10# Alembic, and runs the one-document demo on golden-set/documents/AGR-001.pdf. It never writes keys anywhere.the Azure key is asked for, never stored in git

C.2bOne command installs everything (23 Nov 2026)

SwitchWhat it adds
(none)packages, .env, tables, the PP-OCRv6 OCR model (SHA-256 checked), smoke demo, a list of what is installed

C.3Run in the bank (containers)

  • One compose file: C:\cts-dps\deploy\docker-compose.cts-dps.yml (Docker or Podman; the same images run on Kubernetes later).
  • Every container: non-root, read-only root, no capabilities, CPU and memory limits, health check. Secrets come from the bank's vault at deploy time.
  • Each worker has its own parser container with no network; they share only a socket.
  • Rollback: set DPS_IMAGE_TAG to the previous tag and run the same command (migrations are expand-then-contract).

C.6The scheduler (one leader worker)

  • One worker holds the scheduler lock (dps_leader, lease 60 s, checked every 10 s). It alone pushes events (12.1), ages the queue (every minute), takes back jobs of dead workers and purges old AI answers (DPS_AI_CACHE_DAYS, 30), and seals the audit log (every hour).
  • If the leader dies, another worker takes the lock within 60 s; jobs run on every worker regardless.

66 return self._leader
67 from dps.ops.production import acquire_leader

72 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - a lock hiccup only skips this round of scheduler tasks

C.7Audit, history and logs

  • dps_audit_event: who did what. The code writes these actions: JOB_SUBMIT (api/jobs.py:273), JOB_RETRY (:444), JOB_CANCEL (:459), BATCH_RERUN (:610), JOB_RECLASSIFY (api/review.py:288), LABEL_REMEMBERED (services.py:276), STATEMENT_APPROVED (statement_lines/reader.py:607), and the AI budget alerts (agent/guard.py:105). Review decisions are not here: they are in dps_review_decision.
  • dps_audit_seal: once a day the hash chain over that day's audit events and review decisions, with a file in audit-seals/; /ops/audit-seals re-checks it. A changed row breaks the chain.
  • dps_trace_event: meant as a document's history, but today only one place writes it: history.result when a statement's review is approved (one RESULT row, statement_lines/reader.py:608). No API reads it yet.
  • Logs: JSON per container; the logcollector writes one readable file per day for all containers (secrets masked, 30 days kept).

AlertWhen
DpsInteractiveQueueSlowOldest queued job in {{ $labels.pool }} waited over 5 minutes
DpsScaleOutAdd a {{ $labels.pool }} replica (autoscaling rule)

DpsOverrideRateRisingSampled error rate over 5% for {{ $labels.job_type }}
DpsCalibrationErrorCalibration error above 0.05 for {{ $labels.job_type }}
DpsDeadlocksRisingDatabase deadlocks rising
DpsDerivedDiskFullderived/ disk over 80%
DpsAuditSealLateNo audit seal for 2 days (leader down?)
DpsReviewBacklogHighOver 200 jobs wait for a person (see dps_review_mapping_backlog for mapping review)
DpsReviewWaitLongA job has waited over 24 hours for review
DpsAiUnavailableThe Document Agent's model is failing: documents are read by rules only and sent to review
DpsAiTokensHighModel tokens today over 15 million (check the budget and the cost)

File: C:\cts-dps\deploy\alerts\cts-dps-alerts.yaml

C.9Rollout and go-live

  • Per job type: SHADOW (results stored, not shown: event dps.extraction.shadow), ASSISTED (every field to a person), NORMAL (the thresholds of 10.4). Set in DPS_ROLLOUT_DEFAULT and DPS_ROLLOUT_MODES; each job keeps the mode it ran under.
  • A job type moves to NORMAL only when /ops/go-live shows every target met.

Each is a DPS_... line in C:\cts-dps\dps\.env (template dps\.env.example); defaults and notes from dps\src\dps\settings.py. Azure values use their own names (AZURE_API_BASE, AZURE_API_VERSION, AZURE_DEPLOYMENT, AZURE_API_KEY).
